elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New Section 10.9: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — the cap runs to both Parties, not Vendor only.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap is only "the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim"; there is no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor. To reach preferred, redraft as "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable ... and (b) USD 1,000,000".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: No exclusion of indirect, incidental or consequential damages appears anywhere in the rendered language; Section 10.9 addresses only the aggregate cap and carve-outs.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 10.9 opening: "Except for a Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations ... for which no limitation shall apply".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list names only confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence and willful misconduct; data protection and security obligations are absent and would sit inside the cap.
Section 10.9 carves out "its indemnification obligations ... for which no limitation shall apply".
Section 10.9 carves out "its gross negligence or willful misconduct, for which no limitation shall apply".
Section 10.9 carves out "gross negligence or willful misconduct" from the cap.
Fraud does not appear in the Section 10.9 carve-out list; add "fraud" to the excepted categories for preferred.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in Section 10.9; add "its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights".

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Section 10.9 contains no statement that the Company's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed" — symmetrical application to Company and Vendor; no retained unlimited-Customer-liability language elsewhere.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Cap equals "the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — a 12-month fee basis, no illusory narrow fee definition (no defined "Fees" term is resolved in the Agreement).
Expressly excepted: "its indemnification obligations ... for which no limitation shall apply".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Expressly excepted: "a Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations".
Expressly excepted: "its gross negligence or willful misconduct".
Expressly excepted: "gross negligence or willful misconduct, for which no limitation shall apply".

reasons: The finding of "missing" is corroborated: the rendered original text (Sections 8, 9, 10.8) contains no cap, no exclusive remedy and no consequential-damages exclusion, so a concise insertion is the correct instrument.

Fallback checklist is complete on the face of new Section 10.9: a mutual aggregate cap on a 12-month fee basis with confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence and willful misconduct expressly outside the cap. Position-complete at fallback.

Preferred is not reached: missing the greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, the mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion, and the data protection/security, fraud and IP-infringement carve-outs, plus the statement that Company payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. These are the exact operative additions required to move to preferred.

Minimality holds: a single new subsection is added, nothing existing is deleted or paraphrased, no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no extra damages categories, no procedure and no carve-outs beyond the four fallback elements. Numeric threshold is not exceeded (no volunteered USD floor).

Intent preserved: Section 10.9 is additive, sits after 10.8 in General Provisions, introduces no undefined term ("Company" and "Party" are existing usages), creates no dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict the Warranties or Confidentiality articles.

Drafting nit for the file, not a defect: the cap is anchored to "the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" rather than the preferred "preceding the event giving rise to the claim"; this is acceptable at fallback but should be corrected if we push to preferred.
